The Gators, led by fourth-year head coach [[Todd Golden]], played their home games at the [[O'Connell Center]] in [[Gainesville, Florida]] as members of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). They entered the season as the defending National Champions. ==Previous season== The [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Gators]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with a {{Win-loss record|w=27|l=4}} regular season record, finishing second in the most difficult SEC season in conference history. The Gators got off to a hot start when they finished non-conference play with a {{Win-loss record|w=13|l=0}} record and No. 6 ranking in the AP Poll, which was their highest ranking in 7 years. Despite early losses to [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] and [[2024–25 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]], Florida got hot and finished the regular season winning 9 of their last 10 games. During this stretch, they pulled off massive wins on the road against [[2024–25 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|No. 1 Auburn]] and [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|No. 7 Alabama]]. Led by Clayton Jr. and [[Alex Condon]], Florida was able to beat a No. 1 team on the road for the first time in program history. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]] at [[Bridgestone Arena]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], they defeated [[2024–25 Missouri Tigers men's basketball team|Missouri]], 95–81, in the quarterfinals and [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], 104–82, in the semifinals to advance to the SEC Championship, where they defeated [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 86–77, to clinch their first SEC championship since [[2013–14 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2014]]. They received an automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#West regional – San Francisco, California|West region]]. They defeated [[2024–25 Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball team|Norfolk State]], 95–69, in the first round, [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|two-time]] [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|defending national champions]] [[2024–25 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], 77–75, in the second round, and [[2024–25 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], 87–71, in the Sweet Sixteen to advance to the Elite Eight. There, they defeated [[2024–25 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]], 84–79, to advance to their first Final Four since 2014. They would then defeat SEC rival Auburn, 79–73, to advance to their first [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship]] since 2007. In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], they overcame a 12-point deficit late in the second half to beat [[2024–25 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]], 65–63, to clinch their third national title overall and their first since [[2006–07 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2007]].{{Cite web |last=Pells |first=Eddie |date=2025-04-07
